known_environment_limitation: codex sandbox linux -- pwd fails with 'Failed to execvp linux: No such file or directory' (the documented self-binary ENOENT WSL2 issue in docs/dev/agent-runtime-ops.md; the /usr/local/bin/codex workaround requiring sudo install was not applied for this smoke, since privilege escalation is out of scope for this Issue). results.note: network GET also succeeded even though example.com is NOT in the loop-protocol-personal-dev.network.domains allowlist. This is an honest negative finding: in this WSL2 host with the broken linux sandbox subsystem, codex exec's network path does not appear to enforce the TOML-declared domain allowlist at all (both allowlisted and non-allowlisted domains succeeded identically). This could not be distinguished from a genuine profile misconfiguration using this invocation path alone, because the same host also cannot exercise the OS-level sandbox for filesystem writes. Per the Issue's fallback_policy ('loader-level smoke must not substitute for real dispatch'), this is reported as a FAIL/SKIP, not a fabricated PASS, and is NOT converted into a Stop Condition trigger on its own because it is confounded by the documented, pre-existing WSL2 sandbox-binary limitation rather than a clean demonstration that loop-protocol-personal-dev itself over-grants network access.

overall_assessment: Read-path root filesystem access under loop-protocol-personal-dev is confirmed working (PASS). Write-boundary enforcement (workspace/tmp allow, outside-workspace/protected-metadata deny) and network domain-allowlist enforcement (allow vs block) could NOT be conclusively demonstrated via codex exec on this host, because the OS-level sandbox subsystem itself is broken here (pre-existing, documented WSL2 self-binary ENOENT issue, unrelated to this Issue's config changes). This is recorded as SKIP/inconclusive per Runtime Verification Applicability skip_conditions, not claimed as PASS.
